decision.step: unlisted: take the hollow reading for operator approval
decision.text: D3: after the build is committed, the proof is green under bin/cairn test --netns, and the ticket has crossed PROVEME, take the hollow reading: bin/cairn test --netns --seal --hollow 41202d4c8d3b skills/sail/proofs/test_sail_sweeps_the_tree_first.py. Because the build touched only the proof, the hollow skips it as the instrument and, per ruling 8p (cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py:1100-1110), prints 'ASKED Akien -> open-<id>'; once Akien answers approving, re-run the same command, which prints 'APPROVED ... -> open-<id>' and lands evidence.hollow['41202d4c8d3b'] on the seal. PROVED crosses only after that.

D5: if Akien's answer to the 8p question declines the proofs-only build, the hollow stays red and the ticket does not cross PROVED: it retreats PROVEME->BUILDME, and the decline is folded onto the ticket as a decision line before anything is rebuilt. If he approves, re-run the D3 command and PROVED crosses on its evidence.

D6: the D3 wait is not polled and not guessed. The first --seal run prints one line 'ASKED Akien -> open-<12hex> (cairn question list): once answered, re-run --seal' — copy that id, send it to the peer akiendelllinux_cc_0, and end the turn (no waiter, no loop). Akien's answer is detected by running cairn question show open-<12hex>: it prints the question's JSON, and it is answered exactly when that JSON carries "resolved": true and a non-empty "answer" (his verbatim words) with "answered_by" naming him. An approving answer → re-run the D3 command; the hollow itself re-reads the question (hollow.approval, hollow.py:731) and prints 'APPROVED skills/sail/proofs/test_sail_sweeps_the_tree_first.py -> open-<12hex>' — that printed line, not the builder's reading of his words, is what lands the evidence. If the re-run prints ASKED again (the hollow did not accept the answer as approval), treat it as a decline under D5.

D8: the builder sends the question id to the peer with the Claude Code SendMessage tool, to: 'uds:/run/user/1000/cc-socks/441754.sock' (the peer akiendelllinux_cc_0's socket; if SendMessage is not loaded, load it with ToolSearch 'select:SendMessage'), message: 'ASKED Akien -> open-<12hex> for 41202d4c8d3b hollow (8p)'. Ending the turn alone does NOT communicate it; the send is the act.

D10: measured 2026-10-08 on CairnCommons/questions/open-0aa1abce1583.json, an answered question carries (key order irrelevant; read by key) {"id": "open-0aa1abce1583", "resolved": true, "answered_by": "Akien, recorded by caller class cc", "answer": "<his verbatim words>"}. answered_by names him when it contains 'Akien'. The builder never parses approval out of those words: approval is whatever the D3 re-run's hollow prints (APPROVED vs ASKED), per D6.

decision.step: unlisted: Commit the build and verify it passes the test
decision.text: D12: the build is ALREADY committed (fc17a873 '41202d4c8d3b: build — _sweep_order_problem ...'). Before D3 the builder runs bin/cairn test --netns skills/sail/proofs/test_sail_sweeps_the_tree_first.py and proceeds only on the line '1 proof · 1 green · 0 red' (measured green 2026-10-08); a red stops the voyage and is brought back verbatim. Then it crosses BUILDME->PROVEME with proven_by skills/sail/proofs/test_sail_sweeps_the_tree_first.py (repo-relative path), then runs D3.

D14: the crossing has no CLI verb; it is the library door cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit, called from python with PYTHONPATH=. : new = emit(ticket['workflow_and_state'], 'PROVEME', history_path='skills/sail/history.json', state_path='skills/sail/state.json', ticket='41202d4c8d3b', actor='cc', why='<why>', proven_by=['skills/sail/proofs/test_sail_sweeps_the_tree_first.py']); the returned cursor string is written back onto the ticket's workflow_and_state through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(ticket_path, json.dumps(ticket, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)+'\n', verb='cast', why='<why>'). A refusal from emit is brought back verbatim. The same call with 'BUILDME' and no proven_by is the TICKETME->BUILDME crossing; with 'BUILDME' from PROVEME it is D5's retreat.

D15: a decision is folded onto the ticket with bin/cairn rehearse 41202d4c8d3b --by cc --decide "<step, e.g. D3>" "<the decision line>" — it appends D<n> to the ticket's decisions through the artifact door and prints 'decided D<n> on 41202d4c8d3b ...'. The ticket's bytes change, so the ticket is rehearsed again before the next forward crossing.

D16: emit's why is a one-line statement of what the crossing rests on: for TICKETME->BUILDME 'rehearsal clean at TICKETME:waiting; build already committed fc17a873'; for BUILDME->PROVEME 'proof green under bin/cairn test --netns; build fc17a873 complete'; for D5's retreat 'Akien declined the proofs-only build: <question id>'.

D17: the resume trigger is the peer channel: the builder ends its turn after sending the id, and resumes when the peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 messages that the question is answered (or when a new user/peer message arrives). It then runs cairn question show <id> per D6/D10. No schedule, no poller, no waiter.

D19 (supersedes D8's 'to:' value and all of D13; F34): the peer is addressed by NAME, never by socket. A socket path names one session and is dead when that session ends. At send time the builder calls the ListAgents tool, takes the row whose name is exactly akiendelllinux_cc_0, and calls SendMessage with to: 'akiendelllinux_cc_0' (the bare name, as ListAgents prints it). If no listed row has that name, the builder sends nothing, tries no other address, and stops the voyage there; the stop is reported as a measured stop: 'no peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 listed by ListAgents at <time>'.

decision.text: D20 (F34, as 4784351e4838 D16): D6, D8, D11 and D17 describe the session tooling the voyage runs in (SendMessage, ListAgents, the peer channel, ending the turn). They are not this ticket's build, and this ticket proves nothing about them. Their availability is the session's: if a tool cannot be loaded or a send fails, that refusal is brought back verbatim and the voyage stops; nothing is worked around.

D21 (F34): the wait on Akien's answer to the 8p question is INDEFINITE and has no timeout, no escalation and no default. A timeout on his gate would make the gate advisory. The ticket stays at PROVEME until the question carries his answer (D10); nothing crosses meanwhile.
